summary: Steel tower above Round Pond in the Allagash area. Cab replaced in 2020; a trail guide says do not climb until notified, and a 2020 column says the cabs are open to visitors.

facts.design: Steel tower with a replacement cab (2020), modelled on the Deboullie Mountain cab
facts.agency: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

access.note: A Maine Trail Finder guide says the decommissioned tower should not be climbed until further notice. A 2020 BDN column says hikers can visit the new cabs. The sources disagree; confirm with the Bureau of Parks and Lands.

notes_for_editor: Access conflict is unresolved: the undated Maine Trail Finder guide says the decommissioned tower should not be climbed until further notice, while the 2020 BDN column (by the Allagash superintendent) says the new cabs are for visitors. The record's 2018 'restored' event is recorded here as maintenance and cab planning; the 2020 cab is recorded as 'replaced'. No build date, builder or height found. The 2020 report says the Bureau of Parks and Lands pre-built one cab at its Ashland facility and Shiretown Structures of Houlton built the other two; the column names a local contractor, which is consistent with that, so the builder is treated as resolved. The 2018 report says the Ashland-built cab was for this tower. Access level set to restricted pending the Bureau of Parks and Lands.
